text:
Missoula County podcast discusses open space conservation and community values
H. J. Bell
Missoula County commissioners released a new podcast episode on Aug. 19 focusing on the importance of open space conservation, marking the 20th anniversary of the 2006 city-county bonds that have supported projects such as Marshall Mountain Park and the Rock Creek Confluence.
The commissioners spoke with Jenny Zaso, open lands manager for Missoula County, about how conserving open space serves both as a shared community value and as a valuable tool for private landowners. The discussion highlighted that Missoula voters first approved an open space bond in 1980, establishing a long-standing commitment to land preservation.
Listeners are encouraged to tune in to “The Agenda with the Missoula County Commissioners” or find it wherever they get their podcasts. The episode explores how these initiatives continue to impact local recreation and private property management.
Missoula County enriches local culture by hosting community events at the fairgrounds, supporting educational programs, managing the Rocky Mountain Gardens and Exploration Center at 1075 South Avenue West for community learning and 4H programs, announcing book award winners through its public library, focusing on ecology and public services programs, being led by three elected commissioners who oversee budgets and policy decisions, and promoting safe outdoor burning practices each March 1, all according to the official website.
The county’s efforts reflect ongoing priorities in enhancing both natural spaces and cultural resources for residents.
